newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AIF takes five pct of Melbourne Airport.
newsitem.headline: AIF takes five pct of Melbourne Airport.

text.p: The Australian Infrastructure Fund (AIF) said on Tuesday that it has exercised its option to buy five percent of Australian Pacific Airports Corp Ltd (APAC), the successful tenderer for the Melbourne Airport.
AIF, which is managed by Hastings Funds Management, said it paid about A$18 million for the stake.
Hastings said the unlisted Utilities Trust of Australia, which it also manages, would also acquire five percent of APAC.
The Australian government said on May 7 that it awarded the airport's long term lease to the APAC consortium, which is led by BAA Plc, for a total payment of A$1.307 billion.
BAA said it would have an initial stake of 25.1 percent in APAC but this would fall to 15.1 percent if Hastings exercised its two options.
The other APAC partners are the Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) with a 49.9 percent holding and Sydney-based funds manager Axiom with 25.0 percent.
